lessonRef.title: Writing revision workshop: revising so every integrated claim traces to a note, punctuating quotations from a text

studentTask.text: Today's focus: revising so every integrated claim traces to a note, punctuating quotations from a text. Essential question: How do I investigate a question across sources and record what I found in my own words? By the end of this lesson you should be able to: Revise for development and organization, then edit to the Grade 4 language standards. You'll need: course notebook or an accessible digital equivalent; pencil, keyboard, or another accessible response tool; the assigned passage in print, on screen, or read aloud.

guidedSupport.text:
Work through this with a facilitator, tutor, or on your own if you're ready:
- Welcome and retrieval: Open with a brief accessible retrieval prompt connected to today's lesson. Ask the learner to recall, predict, or pose a question before any instruction.
- Word study and fluency: Two minutes of word work on the vocabulary today's lesson requires, then one short passage read for accuracy and phrasing. Reading aloud is optional.
- Model or mini-lesson: Demonstrate one substantive revision and one editing pass on a sample, never on the learner's assessed draft.
- Guided practice: Read the draft together and identify the weakest-developed section and one convention pattern to fix.

If you get stuck:
- If prerequisite gap: Return to the smallest prerequisite today's lesson depends on, model it once with a text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
- If decoding or fluency barrier: If the barrier is reading the words rather than today's lesson, drop to the word or phrase level, reread the line, then return. Do not reteach today's lesson while decoding is the actual obstacle.
- If repeated error pattern: Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short retrieval check in a later session.

independentEvidenceTask.text: The learner revises that section, then edits for fragments, run-ons, commas, and confused words. When finished: Name the revision you made and the convention you corrected.

- decoding or fluency barrier: If the barrier is reading the words rather than today's lesson, drop to the word or phrase level, reread the line, then return. Do not reteach today's lesson while decoding is the actual obstacle.
- repeated error pattern: Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short retrieval check in a later session.

extension.text: Apply today's lesson to a longer or unfamiliar text, compare two texts on it, or teach it with an original example. Extension never means completing another learner's assessed work.
